Abstract.AbstractText: Pannexins form single membrane channels that regulate the passage of ions, small molecules and metabolites between the intra- and extracellular compartments. In the central nervous system, these channels are integrated into numerous signaling cascades that shape brain physiology and pathology. Post-translational modification of pannexins is complex, with phosphorylation emerging as a prominent form of functional regulation. While much is still not known regarding the specific kinases and modified amino acids, recent reports support a role for Src family tyrosine kinases (SFK) in regulating pannexin channel activity. This review outlines the current evidence supporting SFK-dependent pannexin phosphorylation in the CNS and examines the importance of these modifications in the healthy and diseased brain.
